idea.Name: geometry_lifted_retained_range_som
idea.Title: Geometry-Lifted Retained-Range SOM for Local Pose-Hiding and Reduced Self-Calibration in Full-Wave Inverse Scattering
idea.Short Hypothesis: For unknown antenna pose, the receiver-side Green derivative admits a canonical minimum-norm lift into a retained SOM current space plus an orthogonal irreducible data residual; coupling that lift to the full-wave state equation yields an exact finite-dimensional condition for local pose hiding, and a reduced self-calibration parameterization is lossless for identifiable pose directions while freezing hidden ones.
idea.Related Work: Equivalent currents and contrast sources, classical SOM and twofold SOM, source/receiver-extension full-waveform inversion, inverse scattering with transmitter localization, CSI calibration, blind calibration, SAR/radar autofocus, pseudoinverse lifts, variable projection, and subspace perturbation are established antecedents. The retrieval-bounded contribution is only the type-correct full-wave/SOM synthesis: restrict the geometry-to-current lift to a declared retained current space, retain the orthogonal unrepresentable residual, separate receiver pseudo-current from transmitter-induced physical current, and couple the result to a state-equation rank condition rather than treating the state witness as a pose-quality score.
idea.Abstract: We investigate self-calibrating full-wave inverse scattering when an antenna array pose changes the Green operators used by subspace optimization methods. At the independent-current level we separate receiver-side re-sampling from the physical induced-current change caused by illumination. Given a retained SOM basis, we define the minimum-norm pose-equivalent current by a restricted pseudoinverse and prove an orthogonal decomposition into representable and irreducible data components. Reparameterizing the joint data and state linearization gives an exact finite-dimensional condition for a pose direction to be hidden by retained current and real contrast variations. We retain a full-row-rank negative control and show experimentally in a deterministic 2D scalar Helmholtz solver that unrestricted equivalence is vacuous, while retained-rank lifting is non-vacuous. The completed round verified the orthogonal decomposition, analytic receiver/transmitter/co-moving derivatives, hard-versus-soft spectral filtering, confounded and disambiguated rank regimes, and equivalence of direct joint GN with a geometry-lifted reduced GN in identifiable pose directions while hidden directions remain frozen. The originally proposed state-consistency witness T_U did not discriminate good from bad pose estimates, so it is demoted to a pseudo-current diagnostic and is not used as a reconstruction disambiguator. Planned continuation adds a second frequency/grid or limited-aperture setting, multiple noise seeds, retained-rank and regularization ablations, and an extended transmitter-array check to test whether transmitter-pose calibration can escape the scalar point-source theta gauge. Claims remain local, finite-dimensional, model-conditional, and retrieval-bounded.

datasets: Deterministic synthetic 2D scalar Helmholtz contrast-source scenes on a world-fixed grid using the corrected self-cell quadrature and analytic Green derivatives from the existing project harness.

Single- and multi-pose Tx/Rx arrays with separately controlled receiver-only, transmitter-only, and co-moving SE(2) perturbations; include full-row-rank, deliberately rank-deficient, limited-aperture, and SVD-truncated cases.
Low-dimensional real contrast bases; selected reconstruction points with multiple random noise realizations near the reported 0.032 noise floor and at a higher SNR.
One additional feasible setting: a second frequency or a modestly different grid/discretization, and/or a limited-aperture receiver arc, using the same dense small-grid CPU solver.
If feasible, a small multi-element transmitter array or directional source to test transmitter-pose self-calibration beyond the scalar point-source theta gauge.
baselines: Unrestricted full-current pseudoinverse versus retained-rank SOM lifts, with the full-row-rank negative control retained.
Analytic receiver sampling, physical current, and total pose derivatives versus centered finite differences.
Wrong-pose fixed SOM, direct joint full-wave contrast-pose least squares, and geometry-lifted reduced data-plus-state calibration.
Hard SVD truncation versus a declared soft spectral filter near threshold crossings.
Data-only pose cancellation versus joint data-and-state rank characterization.
Full joint GN versus geometry-lifted reduced GN across retained rank r and regularization/whitening choices.
Identity whitening versus current-norm whitening; fixed small ridge versus adaptive LM.
metrics: Lift reconstruction and orthogonality residuals, irreducible residual norm, lift norm, singular values, cutoff, ranks, and condition numbers.
SOM projector distance/leakage, subspace-bound ratio, spectral gap, threshold-crossing diagnostics, and soft-filter continuity.
Centered finite-difference errors for H_S, physical-current J derivatives, and total B; null-current energy discarded by data-only projection.
Norms and ranks of R_U, D_U, T_U, and stacked pose signature; constructed hidden directions and gauge/anchor controls.
Map error, pose error, data residual, state residual, effective variables, runtime, convergence rate/basin, success counts, and noise sensitivity across multiple seeds.
Rank-transition summary over retained rank r: hidden/visible pose DOF, minimum singular values before/after realification, and reconstruction error breakdown into visible and hidden pose components.
Distribution of the demoted state witness T_U across good and bad pose estimates; reported as a diagnostic with an explicit null result if it still fails to discriminate.
Experiments.compute_estimate: Apple Silicon CPU only. Reuse the existing dense small-grid solver and cached factorizations. Run refinement diagnostics at N=6 or N=8; one additional frequency/grid or limited-aperture setting; multiple noise seeds only for selected reconstruction points. No CUDA, GPU infrastructure, neural training, daemon, database, or web UI.
steps: Read the complete run instructions and theory seed; independently check signs and spaces, and retain the full-row-rank negative control showing unrestricted equivalence is vacuous.

Re-run the completed E1-E5 outcomes as regression checks; demote the state-consistency witness T_U to a pseudo-current diagnostic and explicitly record its distribution across good/bad pose estimates rather than using it as a disambiguator.

Implement the additional setting: a second frequency or a modest grid/limited-aperture configuration, and verify the lift/decomposition and local rank-hiding condition are not artifacts of a single configuration.
Add multiple noise realizations for E5-type reconstruction at identifiable r=4 and mostly hidden r=6 regimes; report median/IQR pose and map errors, success counts, and convergence behavior.

Perform an ablation over retained rank r, regularization/whitening choices, and hard versus soft spectral thresholds; characterize the rank transition from receiver-identifiable to mostly hidden pose and the hidden/visible DOF split.

Attempt an extended transmitter-array or directional-source derivative check and, if stable, a transmitter-pose self-calibration case to determine whether transmitter-pose calibration can escape the scalar point-source theta gauge; otherwise preserve the gauge as an explicit limitation.
Synthesize only executed results and write the paper draft with an originality firewall and explicit limitations, including all negative findings.

Risk Factors and Limitations: The state-consistency witness T_U failed to discriminate good from bad pose estimates in the tested setting; it must remain demoted to a diagnostic and not reappear as a positive disambiguation mechanism.
A full-row-rank unrestricted sensing operator makes every data perturbation current-equivalent; without retaining the restricted-rank lift the central contribution would be vacuous.
The canonical lift depends on whitening, realification, current norm, retained basis, and regularization; it is not metric-free.
Small singular values make the equivalent current unstable, and hard rank thresholds create discontinuous coordinate changes.
Receiver re-sampling produces a pseudo-current, whereas transmitter motion produces a physical induced-current change; combining them before the state equation can double count pose effects.
On a world-fixed homogeneous grid G_D is pose independent; a moving G_D belongs to a different model and is not claimed.
The exact TSOM domain fold is not verified in the project sources, so experiments may use only a truncated SOM basis.
The scalar point-transmitter theta derivative is structurally collinear with tx/ty for all phi0, so transmitter-only pose signature may remain rank 2 even with an anchor angle.
The additional frequency/grid or limited-aperture setting is still synthetic and low-dimensional; it increases breadth but does not prove continuum stability or hardware self-calibration.
The literature screen is retrieval-bounded and source/receiver-extension FWI is a close conceptual antecedent.
A nonlinear benefit may remain initialization-dependent or absent; negative results must remain visible.

report.summary: This round executed E6-E9 in the geometry-lifted retained-range SOM project using the existing 2D scalar Helmholtz harness. E6 showed that an L>=2 rigid transmitter array breaks the scalar point-source theta gauge and enables transmitter-pose self-calibration. E7/E7b tested state-consistent retained-current variants and produced a clean null: the retained-rank state witness still does not discriminate good from bad pose estimates and does not help as a penalty. E8 replicated E5 across 76/76 least-squares runs and two SNR levels, confirming that reduced_r4 is lossless while reduced_r6 freezes hidden pose directions. E9 extended this to N=24/N=32 grids and an alternative scene, with 36/36 runs converged and the same rank/threshold structure. The retained-rank lift is non-vacuous, reduced self-calibration is lossless for identifiable pose directions and freezes hidden ones, and T_U remains diagnostic-only.
key_results: E6 derivative checks: centered finite differences passed at O(eps^2); max relative error 1.9e-7 at eps=1e-4 for the multi-transmitter rigid-array Jacobians.
E6 gauge/rank: one point transmitter has B_t complex rank 2 with theta-column residual ~1.7e-18; L=2 and L=3 transmitter arrays have rank 3 with theta residual 8.9e-4 and 1.2e-3.

E6 nonlinear transmitter-only self-calibration (L=2, N=16, K=3, SNR 30 dB, 4 seeds): wrong-pose baseline pose error 0.1118, theta error 0.05, map error 0.388, residual 0.784; direct/reduced_r4/reduced_r6 recover pose ~1.9e-3, theta ~1.6e-3, map ~5.6e-3 at the 0.030 noise floor.
E6 at SNR 20 dB: direct/reduced variants recover pose ~5.9e-3 and theta ~4.9e-3; co-moving multi-Tx pose error ~1.55e-2.
E7 r=6 confounded single-Tx fixture: direct pose 1.03e-2 with hidden component 9.4e-3; reduced_r6 pose 4.42e-2 with hidden component 4.41e-2 frozen.
E7 hard-cut state_consistent variant froze at p_init because the r=6 cut lands on a degenerate singular-value pair with s6-s7 ≈ 8.7e-19.

E7b soft spectral filter (tanh weights w5=0.982, w6=w7=0.581, w8=0.018) removed the Jacobian blow-up, but no lambda recovered hidden directions: lambda=0 gave retained-data residual 3.5e-5 but pose 0.085, map 0.445, full-data residual 0.462; lambda>=1e-2 collapsed alpha with map ~1.0 and pose ~0.81-0.84.
E7 direct T_U penalty did not help: lambda_T=1e-3 lowered T_U to 0.59-0.69 but produced pose error ~0.52.

E8 replication: 76/76 least-squares runs converged with status 1 and optimality <=1e-10. At SNR 30 zero init: wrongpose pose 1.118e-1 / theta 5.0e-2; direct and reduced_r4 both 7.45e-3 / 3.30e-3; reduced_r6 4.42e-2 / 4.41e-2.
E8 at SNR 20: direct/reduced_r4 2.67e-2 / 7.99e-3; reduced_r6 4.43e-2 / 4.40e-2. reduced_r4 matches direct to solver precision at every seed/SNR, while reduced_r6 is SNR-insensitive and geometric.
E8 perturbed init: reduced_r6 cannot escape its basin (pose 0.150) whereas direct/reduced_r4 reach 1.09e-2.

E9 grids/scenes: N=24 and N=32 base scenes plus an alternative N=16 scene; 36/36 runs converged. r4 is full with n_vis=3; r6 has n_vis=1 and hidden_rank=2 at zero and perturbed init, with two hidden singular values at the ~1e-19 numerical floor.
E9 spectral structure: the s5-s6 pair remains machine-degenerate while neighboring gaps remain ~1e-5 to 1e-4 on every tested grid/scene.

E9 reduced_r4 remains lossless on N=24/N=32 with identical per-run records; the alternative scene is near-lossless with equal residuals. reduced_r6 freezes hidden directions everywhere with pose ~4.3e-2 to 4.6e-2 versus direct ~1.2e-2 to 1.6e-2.
completed_steps: Reused the existing 2D scalar Helmholtz harness and prior result assets.
Implemented and validated an L-transmitter rigid-array forward model with analytic transmitter/receiver/co-moving Jacobians; centered finite differences passed at O(eps^2).
Ran E6 transmitter-only self-calibration for L=2 at multiple SNRs/seeds and a co-moving multi-Tx case.
Ran E7 hard-cut state-consistent retained-current variant and recorded the degenerate r=6 singular-value failure.
Ran E7b soft spectral-filter state-consistent variant across lambda values and documented the pose-flat/scale-incommensurate null.
Tested the original T_U witness as a scalar penalty and recorded that it failed to improve pose estimates.
Ran E8 multi-seed/multi-SNR replication of E5 with 76/76 least-squares runs converged.
Ran E9 larger-grid and alternative-scene experiments with N=24, N=32, and alt N=16; 36/36 runs converged.
Synthesized numeric results from JSON files and printed solver records into the final notes.
dead_ends: The original state-consistency witness T_U did not discriminate good from bad pose estimates and did not participate beneficially as a scalar penalty.
The hard-cut retained-current state_consistent variant at r=6 stopped at the initial point because the SVD cut landed on a degenerate singular-value pair, s6-s7 ≈ 8.7e-19.

The soft-filter state_consistent variant avoided the Jacobian singularity but remained a clean null: lambda=0 gave a physically meaningless optimum, while lambda>=1e-2 collapsed the contrast/pose optimization.
Visual plot inspection was unavailable through the tool; numeric claims are grounded in JSON result files and printed solver records.
next_steps: Strengthen the E6 multi-transmitter result with more seeds, more SNR levels, and possibly directional or element-pattern sources; verify co-moving theta identifiability more tightly.

If state consistency is revisited, use an analytic Jacobian and a properly scale-normalized state residual, or impose hard state equality via variable projection, rather than raw unnormalized data plus scalar T_U penalty.
Add a limited-aperture receiver arc and/or a second frequency to increase breadth.
Consider larger receiver counts M to move away from the M=8 rank edge.
Keep all negative state-witness and hard/soft threshold findings visible in any paper synthesis.

unresolved_issues: The state-consistency witness T_U remains a clean null result: it does not discriminate good from bad pose estimates and does not help as a penalty. The paper must keep it demoted to a diagnostic and not present it as a disambiguation mechanism.

The empirical evidence is still limited to synthetic 2D scalar Helmholtz scenes with small dense grids and CPU solver settings; no limited-aperture receiver arc, real data, or hardware self-calibration is included.

The report summary does not explicitly detail the regularization/whitening ablation from the planned experiments: identity versus current-norm whitening and fixed ridge versus adaptive LM should be reported in the paper if those runs exist.

The transmitter-array result is demonstrated only for L=2 and L=3 rigid arrays; larger arrays or directional-source cases would strengthen the claim that transmitter-pose calibration escapes the point-source theta gauge.

External blind-calibration or source/receiver-extension full-waveform inversion baselines are not compared; direct joint GN is a strong internal baseline, but the paper should clarify the scope relative to those methods.
verdict.reasoning: The study is no longer a pilot or single-setting exploration. E6 provides derivative checks and nonlinear transmitter-only self-calibration across multiple seeds and SNRs, showing that a multi-transmitter rigid array breaks the scalar point-source gauge. E7 and E7b cleanly establish the negative result for the state-consistency witness and the failure of state-consistent penalties to recover hidden directions, without overselling it. E8 replicates the central reduced-rank result across 76/76 least-squares runs and two SNR levels, confirming that reduced_r4 is lossless while reduced_r6 freezes hidden pose directions; perturbed-initialization checks support the basin interpretation. E9 extends the same rank/threshold structure to N=24/N=32 grids and an alternative scene, with 36/36 converged runs and stable spectral degeneracy. There are sensible baselines, ablations over retained rank, hard versus soft spectral filtering, multiple seeds/SNRs, analytic-versus-finite-difference checks, and explicit limitations. The remaining issues are mostly scope limitations or reporting details rather than threats to the central retained-rank lifting and reduced self-calibration claims. This is sufficient for a full-length paper with a rich appendix.
